reason: The sources provide sufficient details to support a short on asteroid 2018 AH.
story: In January 2018, a sub-kilometer asteroid known as 2018 AH zipped past Earth at a distance of roughly 184,500 miles, which is closer than the Moon. Measuring around 100 to 190 meters in diameter—making it comparable in size to the Washington Monument—it was the largest asteroid to pass that close to Earth since 2002 JE9 in 1971. Despite its massive size and proximity, astronomers completely missed it before its closest approach. It was only discovered two days later, on January 4, 2018, by the ATLAS survey on Mauna Loa. The asteroid had approached undetected from the direction of the Sun following perihelion, remaining too dim for standard survey detection until it was gone.
angle: An asteroid the size of the Washington Monument zipped closer than the Moon, and astronomers didn't even notice until two days after it passed.

claims.claim: 2018 AH is an asteroid approximately 100 to 190 meters in diameter.
It was first observed on January 4, 2018.
It was discovered by the ATLAS survey on Mauna Loa.
It passed Earth at a distance of about 297,000 km or 184,500 miles.
This distance is closer than the Moon.
It is the largest asteroid to pass so close to Earth since 2002 JE9 in 1971.
It was discovered two days after its closest approach on January 2, 2018.
It approached Earth from the direction of the Sun.
It is classified as a near-Earth object of the Apollo group.
Precovery observations were found from Pan-STARRS and PTF.
It is not considered a potentially hazardous object by NASA.

disputed: Exact size estimates vary slightly across sources (e.g., 100 meters, 137 meters, or up to 190 meters); a script should state it was roughly the size of the Washington Monument or around 100 to 190 meters.
